title: CUT&Tag-direct for Whole Cells with CUTAC
author: Steven Henikoff
materials: Binding buffer Mix 200 μL 1M HEPES-KOH pH 7.9*, 100 μL 1M KCl, 10 μL 1M CaCl 2 and 10 μL 1M MnCl 2 , and bring the final volume to 10 mL with dH 2 O. Store the buffer at 4 °C for up to several months. *HEPES-NaOH pH 7.5 is OK. Triton-Wash buffer Mix 1 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5, 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl, 12.5 μL 2 M spermidine and 500 µl 10% Triton-X100, bring the final volume to 50 mL with dH 2 O, and add 1 Roche Complete Protease Inhibitor EDTA-Free tablet. Store the buffer at 4 °C for up to 2 days. Antibody buffer Mix 5 µl 200X BSA (optional) and 4 µl 0.5 M EDTA with 1 ml Triton-Wash buffer and chill on ice. BSA is present in some but not all antibody solutions, and 0.1% BSA in this buffer helps to prevent bead loss during later steps. Triton-300-wash buffer Add 750 µL 5M NaCl to 24.3 ml Triton-Wash buffer. Store at 4 °C for up to 2 days. CUT&Tag Tagmentation buffer Mix 1 mL Triton-300-wash buffer and 10 µL 1 M MgCl 2 (to 10 mM). CUTAC-DMF Tagmentation buffer Mix 780 µl dH 2 O, 200 µl N,N-dimethylformamide, 10 µl 1 M TAPS pH 8.5 and 5 µl 1 M MgCl 2 (10 mM TAPS, 5 mM MgCl 2 , 20% DMF). Store the buffer at 4 °C for up to 1 week. TAPS wash buffer Mix 1 mL dH 2 O, 10 µL 1 M TAPS pH 8.5, 0.4 µL 0.5 M EDTA (10 mM TAPS, 0.2 mM EDTA). 1% SDS-ProtK Release solution (For 32 samples) Mix 20 µl 10% SDS and 2 µl 1 M TAPS pH 8.5 in 178 µl dH 2 O. Just before use add 20 µL Thermolabile Proteinase K (NEB cat. no. P8111S). 6% Triton neutralization solution Mix 600 µL 10% Triton-X100 + 400 µL dH 2 O.

To the PCR tube containing the bead slurry add 15 µL of 6% Triton neutralization solution + 2 µL of 10 µM Universal or barcoded i5 primer + 2 µL of 10 µM uniquely barcoded i7 primers, using a different barcode for each sample. Indexed primers are described by Buenrostro, J.D. et al. Single-cell chromatin accessibility reveals principles of regulatory variation. Nature 523:486 (2015). We do not recommend Nextera or NEB primers, which might not anneal efficiently using this PCR protocol.
After the PCR program ends, remove tubes from the thermocycler and add 65 µL of SPRI beads (ratio of 1.3 µL of SPRI beads to 1 L of PCR product). Mix by pipetting up and down.
Let sit at room temperature 5-10 min. 00:05:00

Begin the cycling program with a heated lid on the thermocycler: Cycle 1: 58 °C for 5 min (gap filling) Cycle 2: 72 °C for 5 min (gap filling) Cycle 3: 98 °C for 5 min Cycle 4: 98 °C for 10 sec Cycle 5: 60 °C for 10 sec Repeat Cycles 4-5 11 times 72°C for 1 min and hold at 8 °C To minimize the contribution of large DNA fragments and excess primers, the PCR should be performed for no more than 12-14 cycles, preferably with a 10 s 60-63 °C combined annealing/extension step (Cycle 5). The cycle times are based on using a conventional Peltier cycler (e.g., BioRad/MJ PTC200), in which the ramping times (3 °C/sec) are sufficient for annealing to occur as the sample cools from 98 °C to 60 °C. Therefore, the use of a rapid cycler with a higher ramping rate will require either reducing the ramping time or other adjustments to assure annealing. Do not add extra PCR cycles to see a signal by capillary gel electrophoresis (e.g. Tapestation). If there is no nucleosomal ladder for the H3K27me3 positive control, you may assume that CUT&Tag failed, but observing no signal for a sparse chromatin protein such as a transcription factor is normal, and the barcoded sample can be concentrated for mixing with the pool of barcoded samples for sequencing. Extra PCR cycles reduce the complexity of the library and may result in an unacceptably high level of PCR duplicates. Cycle 3 (98 °C) can be extended from 30 sec to 5 min for cross-linked samples (preferred for CUTAC) to ensure complete cross-link reversal and fragment release.

steps.title: Prepare buffers and reagents
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions: NE1 buffer (1 mL 1 M HEPES‑KOH pH 7.9, 500 µL 1 M KCl, 12.5 µL 2 M spermidine, 500 µL 10 % Triton X‑100, 10 mL glycerol, bring to 38 mL with dH₂O, add one Roche Complete Protease Inhibitor tablet, EDTA‑free); Wash buffer (1 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5, 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl, 12.5 µL 2 M spermidine, bring to 50 mL with dH₂O, add one Roche Complete Protease Inhibitor tablet, EDTA‑free); Binding buffer (as supplied by kit); Antibody buffer (as supplied); Triton‑Wash buffer (as supplied); Triton‑300‑Wash buffer (as supplied); CUTAC‑DMF tagmentation solution (50 µL containing 10 mM TAPS, 5 mM MgCl₂, 20 % DMF); 1 % SDS‑Proteinase K release solution (5 µL per sample); 80 % ethanol; 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8; and keep PBS (1×), 16 % formaldehyde, 1.25 M glycine, DMSO, and any antibodies at hand.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: Collect fresh culture(s) in a 15 mL or 50 mL conical tube at room temperature, count cells, and centrifuge 3 min at 600 × g (swinging‑bucket rotor) at room temperature. Discard supernatant.

steps.title: Wash cells with PBS
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in an equal volume of 1× PBS at room temperature by pipetting up and down, then centrifuge 3 min at 600 × g at room temperature and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Optional light fixation
steps.instruction: While gently vortexing, add 16 % formaldehyde to a final concentration of 0.1 % (e.g., 62 µL to 10 mL PBS) and incubate 2 min at room temperature. Quench by adding 1.25 M glycine to twice the molar amount of formaldehyde (e.g., 600 µL to 10 mL). Centrifuge 4 min at 1300 × g at 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in Wash buffer to a concentration of ~1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹. Check nuclei integrity with a cell counter or ViCell.

steps.title: Optional nuclei freezing
steps.instruction: Aliquot 900 µL nuclei suspension with 100 µL DMSO into cryovials, mix, place in a Mr. Frosty container filled with isopropanol, and store at –80 °C overnight (or longer).

steps.title: Prepare ConA beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend ConA bead slurry, withdraw enough so that 5 µL of beads will be added to each sample (up to ~50 000 cells per sample). Transfer the beads into 1 mL Binding buffer in a 1.5 mL tube, mix by pipetting, place on a magnetic stand for ~1 min, discard supernatant, add 1 mL Binding buffer, mix, magnetise, discard supernatant, and finally resuspend beads in 80 µL Binding buffer (≈4–5 µL per sample). This preparation works for up to 16 samples (80 µL beads) in 1 mL or 32 samples (160 µL beads) in 2 mL Binding buffer.

steps.title: Bind cells to beads
steps.instruction: Transfer up to 60 000 thawed cells or nuclei into each thin‑wall PCR tube, add 5 µL of the prepared ConA beads, attach tubes to a rotator and rotate at room temperature for 10 min. Ensure no more than 5 µL of the original bead suspension is present per tube.

steps.title: Clear beads and remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic stand until beads collect (≈1 min), then withdraw all liquid using a low‑bind wide‑bore 200 µL pipette tip, followed by a quick spin and removal of the last drop with a 20 µL low‑bind tip. Avoid aspirating beads.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Dilute primary antibody 1:25–1:100 in Antibody buffer, add 25–50 µL per sample to the bead‑cell slurry, vortex gently to resuspend, and place on a rotator at room temperature for 1–2 h (or overnight at 4 °C). Include an optional negative control lacking primary antibody.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Magnetise tubes, remove supernatant with a 200 µL low‑bind wide‑bore tip, quick spin, then remove the final drop with a 20 µL low‑bind tip. Add 200 µL Triton‑Wash buffer dropwise while the tube remains on the magnet, then repeat the low‑bind tip removal.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibody at 1:100 in Triton‑Wash buffer, add 25–50 µL per sample while gently vortexing to dislodge beads from the tube walls, and rotate at room temperature for 0.5–1 h.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Quick spin (<500 × g) to collect liquid, place tubes on the magnetic stand, remove supernatant with a 200 µL low‑bind wide‑bore tip, quick spin, then remove the last drop with a 20 µL low‑bind tip. Add 200 µL Triton‑Wash buffer dropwise, then remove supernatant as before.

steps.title: pA‑Tn5 incubation
steps.instruction: Mix pA‑G‑Tn5 pre‑loaded adapter complex in Triton‑300‑Wash buffer according to the manufacturer (e.g., 1:20 for Epicypher CUTANA). Add 25–50 µL per sample, vortex gently, invert by rotation to resuspend beads, quick spin, and rotate at room temperature for 1–2 h.

steps.title: Wash after pA‑Tn5
steps.instruction: Place tubes on the magnetic stand, remove supernatant with a 200 µL low‑bind wide‑bore tip, quick spin, then remove the final drop with a 20 µL low‑bind tip. Add 200 µL Triton‑300‑Wash buffer dropwise, then remove supernatant as above.

steps.title: Tagmentation (CUTAC)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bead/nuclei pellet in 50 µL CUTAC‑DMF tagmentation solution (10 mM TAPS, 5 mM MgCl₂, 20 % DMF), vortex gently, incubate 55 °C for 1 h in a PCR cycler with heated lid, then hold at 8 °C. Proceed to the next wash step.

steps.title: Tagmentation (CUT&Tag)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bead/nuclei pellet in 50 µL standard tagmentation solution, vortex, quick spin (<500 × g), incubate 37 °C for 1 h in a PCR cycler with heated lid, then hold at 8 °C. Proceed to the next wash step.

steps.title: Post‑tagmentation wash
steps.instruction: Place tubes on the magnetic stand, remove supernatant with a 200 µL low‑bind wide‑bore tip, then resuspend beads in 50 µL TAPS wash.

steps.title: SDS‑Proteinase K release
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 5 µL 1 % SDS‑Proteinase K release solution, vortex vigorously to cover beads stuck to tube sides, quick spin, then incubate 37 °C for 1 h followed by 58 °C for 1 h in a PCR cycler (Proteinase K digestion and enzyme inactivation).

steps.title: Add PCR mix
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL NEBNext (non‑hot‑start) PCR master mix, vortex to mix, quick spin, and place tubes immediately in a thermocycler for PCR amplification (program as per kit instructions).

steps.title: Post‑PCR bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic stand for a few minutes until solution clears, remove and discard supernatant, keep tubes on the magnet and add 200 µL 80 % ethanol, let stand, then repeat the ethanol wash. Perform a quick spin, remove remaining supernatant with a 20 µL tip, and proceed without allowing beads to air‑dry.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from the magnet, add 22 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, vortex at full speed, let sit 5 min to 1 h, place on magnetic stand until clear, then transfer the eluate to a fresh 1.5 mL tube, avoiding bead transfer.

steps.title: Library quality control
steps.instruction: Determine library size distribution and concentration using an Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 reagents (or equivalent). Dilute each library to 2 nM based on fragment molarity in the 175–1000 bp range.

steps.title: Pool barcoded libraries
steps.instruction: Mix barcoded libraries in equal molar amounts to achieve the desired final concentration (as recommended by the sequencer manufacturer). Perform an SPRI bead cleanup if residual PCR primers need removal.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the pooled libraries on an Illumina platform using paired‑end reads (PE25 or PE50; PE50 is sufficient for most genomes).
